text.p: Cincinnati Bell Inc said its information systems unit, CBIS, won a contract extension with 360 Communications Co (formerly Sprint Cellular) worth an estimated $600 million.

The service agreement under which CBIS provides billing and customer service for 360 originally was for six years. Now it will run until the year 2006, Cincinnati Bell president and chief executive officer John LaMacchia said in a interview.
The worth of the 10-year contract is "a forecast, hopefully reliable and ... conservative," he said.
He did not disclose the value of the original contract.

LaMacchia said the extended contract provides the opportunity for 360 to migrate to CBIS's UNIX-based Precedent 2000 product, which he said is a modern client server-based software billing system which 360 and CBIS have tested.
"360 is one of our oldest wireless clients in CBIS and was the first to step up to trialing our Precedent 2000 product," he said.
CBIS believes that product could revolutionize billing efficiency for the wireless and possibly other telecommunications sectors, he added.

Cincinnati-based CBIS produces more than 225 million bills a year for clients in cable television, wireless and other telecommunications sectors. 360, a cellular phone service company based in Chicago, has 1.75 million customers in 14 states, Cincinnati Bell said.
